prize_parts.citation: for the development of targeted protein degradation, in which small molecules redirect the ubiquitin-proteasome system to destroy chosen proteins, through the PROTAC concept and the identification of cereblon as the target of molecular glues

statement.case_for: After the full first-round exchange I keep B045 as my preferred configuration with the same three names. The scientific core is unchanged: a small molecule that brings a target and an E3 ligase together turns inhibition into event-driven, catalytic removal, and this is a designable chemical principle (induced proximity, ternary-complex cooperativity) that makes targets without a druggable pocket approachable. Crews and Deshaies supplied the heterobifunctional concept and first proofs; Handa identified cereblon, which explained thalidomide and gave the field its most used ligase handle. The round-1 record shows that six of eight members place B045 in their first choice or alternatives, and no other ballot has that breadth, but I do not treat that count as the argument. The argument is that the principle is confirmed by many independent groups with structures and degradation kinetics, and that the molecular-glue branch already has approved drugs while the PROTAC branch has clinical-stage compounds. I would word the citation so that it openly credits a concept and a mechanism, not the later optimisation work.
statement.case_against: The reservations raised by Somfai, Zou, Sparr, Brzezinski and Aqvist are real and I do not dismiss them. No PROTAC is approved, so the clinical verdict on the bifunctional branch is still pending. The three-name cut excludes Ciulli (VHL ligands, ternary-complex structure), Gray, Sakamoto, Kim and Ito, and the PROTAC and glue strands were discovered separately, so a single citation risks blurring two achievements. If the committee decides the two strands cannot honestly share one citation, or that a trio is indefensible, B045 should wait and a mature candidate such as B069 is the legitimate alternative.

responses.point: Somfai and Zou argue that B069 has the cleanest attribution and more than 25 years of confirmation, and that B045 should not outrank a mature method while credit is split between two strands.
responses.response: I accept that B069 is the safest prize on the list on attribution and maturity, and I keep it as my first alternative for that reason. I still weigh generative reach more heavily: C-N coupling made an existing bond construction routine, whereas degradation changed what can be targeted at all, and the glue branch shows the consequence is not merely prospective. On your credit point, I would answer the two-strand worry by writing the citation to name both the PROTAC concept and cereblon explicitly, and by accepting that the three names are a deliberate choice of concept and mechanism, not a claim that nobody else mattered. If a majority wants certainty over novelty I would not regard B069 as a poor outcome.

responses.point: Zou would rank B045 behind B069 because general rules for productive degradation are not settled, the clinical evidence is pending, and Ciulli and Gray are excluded.
responses.response: You are right that predictive rules for productive ternary complexes are incomplete, but the same was true of many methods when they were recognised; what matters for the prize is that the principle is reproducible and used. Thalidomide analogues acting through cereblon are already approved and widely used, and that is the clearest evidence that the induced-proximity mechanism delivers in patients. I concede that the PROTAC branch is less mature than the glue branch, which is why I want the citation to say what is being rewarded. I do not agree that waiting for an approved PROTAC is the right threshold, but I would want the expert reports to state the status of the clinical evidence.

responses.point: Aqvist prefers B009 for demonstrated global impact and says B045 is the better-supported alternative if a three-name cut for lipid nanoparticles cannot be defended.
responses.response: We agree that the attribution for B009 is the obstacle: the Vancouver strand (Cullis, Hope, Madden, MacLachlan) and the MIT strand (Anderson, Langer) cannot be split in three without excluding someone whose work was decisive, and the patent history adds to it. I move B009 out of my alternatives for that reason and replace it with B069, which has a cleaner credit. Your own statement that B045 is the better alternative is useful, because it suggests the committee can converge on degraders if the credit and citation are handled carefully.

responses.point: Chabes supports the same Crews, Deshaies, Handa trio and a citation naming both bifunctional degraders and molecular glues, and would name Liu alone for base editing.
responses.response: I agree with the trio and with a citation that names both strands. On Handa versus Ciulli, I keep Handa because cereblon is a different kind of discovery, an unexpected mechanism for an existing drug, not an improvement of the PROTAC design, while Ciulli's VHL work is optimisation of the first concept even though it was important. I accept your point on B026: a base-editing prize would follow the CRISPR prize closely and the overlap with the Nishida and Kondo editor is unresolved, so I keep it only as a second alternative and I am no longer pressing the Komor and Gaudelli names.

responses.point: Sparr prefers B008 for a new physical-chemical concept of membraneless organisation and argues that phase separation is as widely replicated as degradation.
responses.response: I value the concept and our shared interest in self-assembly, but the question I would need answered is whether in vivo condensates are equilibrium liquid-liquid phase separation, and the committee's own record calls that contested. The credit also forces a choice among Hyman, Brangwynne, Rosen, Pappu and Mittag. Degradation has a precise mechanistic definition and a clear set of discoverers for its two strands, which makes it easier to cite honestly today. I would revisit B008 once the definition and in vivo evidence settle.

responses.point: The chair asks whether Ciulli displaces Handa, whether the strands are one discovery, and what evidence would make B045 count as mature.
responses.response: Ciulli should not displace Handa in a three-name cut, and a two-part structure would not help because it would only move the same dispute. I regard the strands as one platform whose common principle is induced proximity; the citation should say that the concept and the cereblon mechanism are what is rewarded. For maturity, I would count the approved cereblon-based drugs plus the independent structural and kinetic confirmation as sufficient, and I would not need an approved PROTAC.

uncertainties: Whether the committee will accept awarding degraders before a PROTAC has been approved, and whether the cereblon-based approved drugs are enough to count as maturity.
Whether a single citation can honestly cover the PROTAC concept and the cereblon mechanism without implying Handa's work is a PROTAC advance.
Whether excluding Ciulli, Gray, Sakamoto, Kim and Ito is defensible, or whether the committee decides no trio is fair.
I cannot independently verify the current clinical status of degraders.
statement.conflict_note: No conflict with any shortlisted candidate. My research is on peptides, nanoparticle biosensing and biomaterials, with no collaboration or institutional tie to the credited persons of B045, B069, B026 or B009; my postdoc mentors (Stevens, Boey) are not on the shortlist. I share some research overlap with Emma Sparr on self-assembly relevant to B008, which is not at recusal level and does not affect my position. Round 1 raised nothing that changes this disclosure.
